AI Act.Art. 2(1): Scope: the Act applies to providers placing AI systems on the EU market, to deployers in the EU, and to providers and deployers elsewhere when the output is used in the EU.
AI Act.Art. 2(8): Research, testing and development before a system is placed on the market or put into service are outside the Act (testing in real-world conditions is not).
AI Act.Art. 2(10): Purely personal, non-professional use by a person is excluded.
AI Act.Art. 2(12): Systems released under free and open-source licences are excluded unless they are high-risk, prohibited or fall under Art. 50.
AI Act.Art. 3(1): Definition: an AI system is a machine-based system that operates with some autonomy and infers from its input how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions.
AI Act.Art. 3(3): Definition: a provider develops an AI system, or has one developed, and puts it on the market or into service under its own name.
AI Act.Art. 3(4): Definition: a deployer uses an AI system under its authority in a professional activity.
AI Act.Art. 3(34): Definition: biometric data is personal data from technical processing of a person's physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics, such as faces or fingerprints.
AI Act.Art. 3(39): Definition: emotion recognition infers a person's emotions or intentions from their biometric data.
AI Act.Art. 3(63): Definition: a general-purpose AI model can perform a wide range of tasks and be built into many systems.
AI Act.Art. 4: AI literacy: providers and deployers take measures so that the staff who work with AI understand it well enough for their task.
AI Act.Art. 4a: Special categories of personal data may be processed to detect and correct bias, under strict conditions (added by the 2026 amendment).
AI Act.Art. 5: Prohibited AI practices (Unacceptable risk): the Act bans, for example, manipulative techniques, exploiting vulnerabilities, social scoring, emotion inference in workplaces and schools, and some biometric uses.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(a): Banned: subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques that materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(b): Banned: exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(c): Banned: social scoring that leads to detrimental or disproportionate treatment.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(d): Banned: assessing the risk that a person commits a crime based only on profiling or personality traits.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(e): Banned: building facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping of images.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(f): Banned: inferring the emotions of people in the workplace or in education from their biometric data, except for medical or safety reasons.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(g): Banned: biometric categorisation that deduces race, political opinions, trade-union membership, religion or sexual orientation.
AI Act.Art. 5(1)(h): Banned: real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement, outside narrow exceptions.
AI Act.Art. 6(1): High-risk through products: a safety component of a product, or a product itself, covered by the EU product laws in Annex I that needs third-party conformity assessment.
AI Act.Art. 6(2): High-risk through purpose: a system whose intended purpose is in an area listed in Annex III is high-risk.
AI Act.Art. 6(3): Exception: an Annex III system is not high-risk if it poses no significant risk, for example because it only does a narrow or preparatory task. A system that profiles people is always high-risk.
AI Act.Art. 6(3)(a): Exception condition: the system performs a narrow procedural task.
AI Act.Art. 6(3)(b): Exception condition: the system improves the result of a previously completed human activity.
AI Act.Art. 6(3)(c): Exception condition: the system detects decision patterns or deviations and is not meant to replace or influence a human assessment without proper human review.
AI Act.Art. 6(3)(d): Exception condition: the system performs a preparatory task for an assessment relevant to an Annex III use case.
AI Act.Art. 6(4): A provider who relies on the Art. 6(3) exception documents its assessment before placing the system on the market.
AI Act.Art. 9: High-risk providers: operate a risk management system.
AI Act.Art. 10: High-risk providers: data and data governance for training, validation and test data.
AI Act.Art. 11: High-risk providers: draw up technical documentation.
AI Act.Art. 12: High-risk systems: automatic recording of events (logging).
AI Act.Art. 13: High-risk providers: transparency and instructions for use for deployers.
AI Act.Art. 14: High-risk systems: designed so that people can oversee them effectively.
AI Act.Art. 15: High-risk systems: appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.
AI Act.Art. 16: High-risk providers: overall duties, including quality management, conformity assessment, declaration, CE marking and registration.
AI Act.Art. 17: High-risk providers: operate a quality management system.
AI Act.Art. 25(1): A deployer or distributor becomes the provider of a high-risk system if it puts its own name on it, substantially modifies it, or changes its purpose so that it becomes high-risk.
AI Act.Art. 26(1): High-risk deployers: use the system according to its instructions.
AI Act.Art. 26(2): High-risk deployers: assign human oversight to competent, trained people with authority.
AI Act.Art. 26(4): High-risk deployers: make sure input data is relevant and representative, where they control it.
AI Act.Art. 26(5): High-risk deployers: monitor operation and inform the provider and authorities of risks and serious incidents.
AI Act.Art. 26(6): High-risk deployers: keep the automatically generated logs for at least six months.
AI Act.Art. 26(7): High-risk deployers who are employers: inform workers' representatives and affected workers before use at the workplace.
AI Act.Art. 26(11): High-risk deployers: inform people that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them.
AI Act.Art. 27: Fundamental rights impact assessment before first use, for public bodies, providers of public services and some credit and insurance uses.
AI Act.Art. 43: High-risk providers: conformity assessment before the system is placed on the market.
AI Act.Art. 47: High-risk providers: an EU declaration of conformity.
AI Act.Art. 49: High-risk providers: register the system in the EU database.
AI Act.Art. 49(2): A provider who relies on the Art. 6(3) exception registers the system in the EU database.
AI Act.Art. 50(1): Transparency: systems that interact directly with people must make clear that they are AI, unless that is obvious.
AI Act.Art. 50(2): Transparency: systems that generate synthetic text, audio, image or video must mark the output as artificially generated in a machine-readable way, unless they only assist standard editing.
AI Act.Art. 50(3): Transparency: deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform the people exposed to them.
AI Act.Art. 50(4): Transparency: deployers disclose deepfakes, and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.
AI Act.Art. 50(5): Transparency information is given clearly, at the latest at the first interaction or exposure.
AI Act.Art. 53: General-purpose AI model providers: technical documentation, information for downstream providers, a copyright policy and a summary of the training data.
AI Act.Art. 55: Extra duties for general-purpose AI models with systemic risk.
AI Act.Art. 86: Affected people can ask for an explanation of the system's role in a decision with legal or similarly significant effects.
AI Act.Art. 95: Voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged for systems that are not high-risk.
AI Act.Art. 99(3): Fines for prohibited practices: up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover.
AI Act.Art. 99(4): Fines for most other duties, including high-risk duties and Art. 50: up to EUR 15 million or 3%.
AI Act.Art. 99(5): Fines for incorrect or misleading information to authorities: up to EUR 7.5 million or 1%.
AI Act.Art. 99(6): For SMEs and start-ups the lower of the two fine amounts applies.
AI Act.Art. 111(2): High-risk systems already on the market before their application date are caught only if their design changes significantly afterwards.
AI Act.Art. 113: Sets when the Act applies; the application dates are listed in the reference.
AI Act.Annex I: Annex I: EU product laws, for example for medical devices, toys, lifts, radio equipment, pressure equipment, vehicles and aviation.
AI Act.Annex III: Annex III: the list of high-risk areas: biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration and border control, and justice and democratic processes.
AI Act.Annex III(1): High-risk area 1, biometrics: remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation by sensitive characteristics, and emotion recognition.
AI Act.Annex III(1)(a): Biometrics: remote biometric identification systems (not mere verification that a person is who they claim to be).
AI Act.Annex III(1)(b): Biometrics: categorisation of people according to sensitive or protected attributes.
AI Act.Annex III(2): High-risk area 2, critical infrastructure: safety components in critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, and the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
AI Act.Annex III(3): High-risk area 3, education and vocational training: admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing the level of education, and monitoring cheating in tests.
AI Act.Annex III(3)(a): Education: determining access or admission, or assigning people to institutions.
AI Act.Annex III(3)(b): Education: evaluating learning outcomes, including when used to steer the learning process.
AI Act.Annex III(3)(c): Education: assessing the appropriate level of education a person will receive or can access.
AI Act.Annex III(3)(d): Education: monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests.
AI Act.Annex III(4): High-risk area 4, employment and workers' management: recruitment and selection, decisions about work terms, promotion and termination, task allocation, and monitoring and evaluating workers.
AI Act.Annex III(4)(a): Employment: recruitment or selection, such as targeted job ads, filtering applications and evaluating candidates.
AI Act.Annex III(4)(b): Employment: decisions about terms of work, promotion or termination, allocating tasks by individual behaviour, and monitoring and evaluating the performance and behaviour of people at work.
AI Act.Annex III(5): High-risk area 5, essential private and public services: public benefits, creditworthiness, life and health insurance pricing, and emergency calls and triage.
AI Act.Annex III(5)(a): Essential services: used by or for public authorities to evaluate eligibility for essential public benefits and services.
AI Act.Annex III(5)(b): Essential services: evaluating the creditworthiness of people or setting their credit score (except fraud detection).
AI Act.Annex III(5)(c): Essential services: risk assessment and pricing for people in life and health insurance.
AI Act.Annex III(5)(d): Essential services: evaluating and classifying emergency calls, dispatching emergency services, and emergency healthcare triage.
AI Act.Annex III(6): High-risk area 6, law enforcement: risk assessments of people, polygraphs, evaluating evidence, and profiling in investigations.
AI Act.Annex III(6)(a): Law enforcement: assessing the risk of a person becoming a victim of crime.
AI Act.Annex III(6)(b): Law enforcement: polygraphs and similar tools.
AI Act.Annex III(6)(c): Law enforcement: evaluating the reliability of evidence.
AI Act.Annex III(6)(d): Law enforcement: assessing the risk of offending or re-offending, or a person's personality traits and past criminal behaviour.
AI Act.Annex III(6)(e): Law enforcement: profiling of people in detecting, investigating or prosecuting crime.
AI Act.Annex III(7): High-risk area 7, migration, asylum and border control: risk assessments, examination of applications, and detecting or identifying people.
AI Act.Annex III(7)(b): Migration: assessing a security, irregular-migration or health risk of a person who intends to enter or has entered a Member State.
AI Act.Annex III(7)(c): Migration: assisting the examination of asylum, visa and residence permit applications and related complaints.
AI Act.Annex III(7)(d): Migration: detecting, recognising or identifying people, except verifying travel documents.
AI Act.Annex III(8): High-risk area 8, justice and democratic processes: judicial authorities, and influencing elections or voting behaviour.
AI Act.Annex III(8)(a): Justice: used by or for a judicial authority to research and interpret facts and law and to apply the law to facts.
AI Act.Annex III(8)(b): Democratic processes: intended to influence the outcome of an election or referendum or people's voting behaviour.

GDPR.Art. 6: GDPR Art. 6: processing personal data needs a legal basis.
GDPR.Art. 9: GDPR Art. 9: special categories of personal data, such as health, biometric, trade-union or religious data, have stricter conditions.
GDPR.Art. 22: GDPR Art. 22: people have a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects.
GDPR.Art. 28: GDPR Art. 28: a processor that handles personal data on your behalf needs a contract.
GDPR.Art. 35: GDPR Art. 35: a data protection impact assessment is needed for high-risk processing of personal data.
GDPR.Art. 44: GDPR Art. 44: transfers of personal data outside the EU need safeguards.
